title: MRI edema grades improve retrospective neural-network prognosis for Guillain–Barré syndrome
summary: A two-institution retrospective study used a shallow neural network to estimate residual symptoms six months after discharge in 354 Guillain–Barré syndrome patients. Adding radiologist-assigned lumbosacral edema grades to clinical variables increased the source-reported external-cohort AUC from 0.84 to 0.97. The model includes a muscle-strength score measured at discharge, so it is not an admission-only forecast. External testing used 118 patients from a second institution; treatment benefit and prospective deployment were not tested.
organization: Shandong University; Shandong First Medical University

evidence.tested: Retrospective development on 236 patients and external testing on 118; source reports external AUC 0.84 for clinical variables versus 0.97 with MRI grading. MRI reader agreement was assessed separately.
evidence.unknown: The predictor includes discharge muscle strength and does not establish early admission-only utility. Retrospective selection and source reporting inconsistencies limit interpretation; no causal or treatment benefit is inferred.
evidence.ai_role: A shallow neural network learned six-month outcome classification from clinical factors, with and without radiologist-assigned MRI edema grades; comparison isolates the added predictive information in the MRI grade.

source_review.scope: Exact primary article-front DOI/title/PMCID and date; full relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; fresh PubMed publication types and correction/retraction relationship metadata.
